finding.claim: Unvalidated fetch of attacker-supplied URL in /fetch handler; response body is returned to the caller.

trace.note: io.Copy writes upstream response body back to attacker

finding.guards_checked: None. No host, IP, scheme, or redirect validation. Go's client only supports http/https, which does not restrict destination; loopback, RFC1918, and cloud metadata (169.254.169.254) are reachable and readable.

verdict.guard_found: none on the /fetch path. main.go:14-23 (fetch) has no host, scheme, or IP validation before http.Get at main.go:16. The allowlist at main.go:9-12 and its check at main.go:27 belong to safeFetch (main.go:25-38), which is registered on a separate route (/safe, main.go:42) and is not on the /fetch path.
verdict.reason: The target value comes from the query string at main.go:15, which an unauthenticated caller controls; it reaches http.Get at main.go:16 with no validation, and the response body is copied back to the caller at main.go:22. All trace lines match the code, and the only allowlist is in the separate safeFetch handler, so it does not close this path.

finding.claim: Allowlist check in /safe validates only the initial URL; default http.Client follows redirects, so an allowlisted host that redirects can reach internal addresses. Conditional on an open redirect on an allowlisted host.

trace.note: exact hostname match against allowed map; err checked before u is dereferenced
http.Get on DefaultClient, which follows up to 10 redirects with no CheckRedirect
io.Copy returns response body from redirect target to attacker

finding.guards_checked: err check before deref (ok); exact Hostname allowlist (ok, rejects #@, backslash, port and case tricks; no parser differential since Go's parse and String round-trip the same host); scheme enforced by net/http (ok). Missing: redirect-hop revalidation and dial-time IP blocking. Exploitability depends on an open redirect or attacker-influenced response on images.example.org or docs.example.org. Based on reading Go net/http defaults, not executed.

verdict.guard_found: main.go:27 exact hostname membership on the parsed initial URL (`allowed[u.Hostname()]`), short-circuited after the err check. No CheckRedirect or redirect-hop validation exists anywhere in main.go, and the client at main.go:31 is http.Get, which uses DefaultClient and follows redirects.
verdict.reason: The trace is accurate: the query param reaches the sink at main.go:31 and the allowlist at main.go:27 closes only the initial URL, while http.Get at main.go:31 follows redirects with no revalidation. Whether that is exploitable depends on an open redirect on images.example.org or docs.example.org, which is outside this repo and cannot be checked from the code, so the redirect bypass is not confirmed here.
